description: Sustained malformed-input load (driver: radamsa over H1 OR a Jazzer in-process driver) followed by cooldown + forced GC. Measures process RSS delta, native-heap committed delta (when NMT enabled on the target), and MemoryAllocator.stats().leakCount() delta (when the target exposes the diagnostic endpoint). PASS: deltas within tolerance. FAIL (degradation_class=leak-suspected): RSS delta correlates with attack duration, i.e. each error path that fails to close its Arena pinches a buffer permanently.

attack_profile.rate_note: 500 rps x 600 s = 300 000 iterations. Under the pre-2026-08-26 single-threaded driver that was ~24 h of wall clock at the achieved 3.4 rps, so this scenario could not run as written -- it was blocked on the driver, not on the target. requests_per_second is a REQUESTED rate. Until 2026-08-26 the driver was single-threaded and every read timeout blocked it for the full socket deadline, so the first campaign requested 500 and achieved 3.4 (60 timeouts x 2.0 s consumed the whole 120 s window; radamsa generation was 1.1 % of it). The driver now fires from a worker pool and reports achieved_rps and backlog_skips -- a run that cannot reach this rate says so instead of letting this number stand in for what happened.
attack_profile.concurrency_note: Concurrency is part of the stimulus, not a harness detail: N connections at once is a different attack from N in sequence. It travels with the result and belongs in any comparison. Sizing: rps x incomplete-mutant fraction x socket timeout gives the worker-seconds per wall second the timeouts alone consume.

instrumentation.rss_sampling: MANDATORY — before attack, end of attack window, post-cooldown after forced GC
instrumentation.jcmd_nmt: OPTIONAL — captured when target was launched with -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary or detail
instrumentation.jfr_recording: RECOMMENDED — jdk.ObjectAllocationSample + jdk.JavaMonitorEnter + custom Arena lifecycle events if instrumented in kernel

tolerance.rss_note: rss_growth_pct_max is measured against a baseline taken AFTER a warm-up (baseline_warmup_seconds in the artifact). Before 2026-08-26 the baseline was cold, so first-load JIT, metaspace fill and heap commit were charged to the attack: the first slowloris run read +34.9 % against this 5 % bound while its JFR put live heap after the forced GC at 9.5 MB. RSS remains a weak leak signal here -- see comparison_axis_note -- and a run without NMT leaves the non-heap remainder unattributed. Do not compare rss_bytes_delta across runs with different baseline_warmup_seconds. Both samples are additionally preceded by a forced GC (since 2026-08-27), so the delta compares two post-collection states -- retained memory. Before that date only the FINAL sample was, which compared a collected heap against an uncollected one and biased the delta toward understating growth; on destructive-radamsa-h2 it read -588 517 376 bytes. Artifacts from before that change are not comparable with later ones.

comparison_axis_note: RSS growth tolerance is target-specific. A target with a fixed off-heap pool will show ~0% growth regardless of leaks (leaks materialize as pool exhaustion, not RSS growth). For pool-backed targets, prefer MemoryAllocator.stats().leakCount() over RSS as the primary signal.
